QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_44

question.text: The futures settlement price of a 6.5% coupon government bond futures contract is Rs 103 (i.e., SP = 103), and the conversion factor (CF) for the deliverable bond is 0.98. Using the NISM Series IV bond-futures formula (p.250), what is the clean invoice price the buyer pays at delivery, EXCLUDING accrued interest?

answer.text: Rs 100.94 (Clean invoice = Futures settlement price x CF = 103 x 0.98)
Rs 103.00 (treating SP as the invoice price without applying CF)

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series IV p.250 defines the invoice price for bond futures as: Invoice Price = Futures Settlement Price x Conversion Factor + Accrued Interest. The stem asks for the CLEAN invoice (excluding accrued interest), so Clean Invoice = SP x CF = 103 x 0.98 = Rs 100.94. The CF normalises the futures price to the specific deliverable bond. The Trap: Rs 103.00 ignores the CF entirely. Dividing by CF (Rs 105.06) inverts the formula. Using a CF of 0.99 (Rs 101.97) is an arithmetic error. The audit flagged the original stem because it described the bond as "priced at Rs 103", which read as the cash/market bond price; the formula requires the futures settlement price, so the keyed Rs 100.94 only follows if Rs 103 is the futures SP. Note: The original stem said the bond was "priced at Rs 103", which read as a cash/market bond price rather than the futures settlement price required by the workbook formula. The stem has been tightened to expressly state SP = 103 (futures settlement price) and to ask for the clean invoice (excluding accrued interest), so 103 x 0.98 = Rs 100.94 is uniquely consistent with NISM Series IV p.250.
